newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foreign investment in Taiwan up 46 pct in Jan-Feb.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Taiwan up 46 pct in Jan-Feb.

text.p: Foreign investment in Taiwan surged a year-on-year 46 percent in January-February, reflecting efforts to transform the island into an Asia-Pacific hub for transnational companies, officials said on Tuesday.
In the first two months of 1997, foreign investment totalled US$324 million, up 46 percent from $221 million from the same 1996 period, the Investment Commission said.
Foreign investment in the electronics and electrical appliance industries, which topped the investment sector with 25 percent of the pie, accounted for $80.05 million, up 56 percent, it said.
Investment in the next biggest sector, international trade, grew 116 percent, while investment in services grew 232 percent and that in chemicals manufacturing rose 422 percent.
Investment in the finance and insurance industry fell 41 percent, it said.
Broken down by origin, investment from unspecified "other regions" leapt 114 percent to $120.5 milion, followed by the United States, which rocketed 343 percent to $66.4 million.
Investment from Japan fell 30 percent to $48 million, while that from Europe surged 200 percent to $36.5 million and that from Hong Kong rose 21 percent to $13.7 million.
Taiwan's own overseas investments, excluding mainland China, fell 32 percent in January-February to $153.8 million from $226.5 million in the 1996 period.
January-February investment by Taiwan in unspecified "other regions" -- mainly tax havens in central America -- dropped 83 percent to $69.2 million.
Taiwan's U.S. investments slid 13 percent to $28.1 million.
Investment in southeast Asia surged in January-February as Taiwan businesses have been urged by the government to diversify their investments away from the communist Chinese mainland.

Worried that Taiwan firms could become too dependent on the island's principal adversary, leaving Taiwan politically vulnerable, Taipei launched a "southbound policy" in late 1993 to promote investments in Southeast Asia instead of China.
January-February investment in Vietnam surged an annual 76 percent to $37.1 million, followed by the Philippines, which leapt 94 percent to $12.5 million.
Investment in Indonesia rocketed 3,625 percent to $3.91 million. Investment in Thailand rose 24 percent, but investment in Malaysia and Singapore both fell 98 percent.
Overseas investments focused on foods and beverages, electronics and electrical appliance, finance and insurance, retail and transport industries, it said.
